ratings.heading: Average of 2 booking sites, weighted by number of reviews

pills.label: 70–130 minutes
pills.pop_html: Duration: 70–130 minutes.
Who plays: organist Teleki Miklós, bass singer Kolos Kováts (Liszt Ferenc Prize and Kossuth Prize holder) and flautist Eleonóra Krusic. It is a trio, not an orchestra.

Programme: Mozart's Fantasie in F minor, Stradella's Pietà Signore, Albinoni's Adagio, Liszt's St Francis Legend, Verdi's Prayer of Fiesco, Bach's Badinerie suite, and it closes with Bach's Toccata and Fugue in D minor.
Where you sit: VIP is the 1st row, Category I rows 2–6, Category II rows 7–16, Category III rows 17–26. Each category is priced separately, so check which rows your ticket covers before you pay.
The venue: the concert is held inside St Stephen's Basilica on Szent István tér, a neo-classical church known for its acoustics.

pills.label: What's included
pills.pop_html: Included: Concert ticket.

best_for.pick_html: for a first evening in Budapest, because €26 gets you Bach's Toccata and Fugue on the Basilica organ with two soloists, at half the price of the other Basilica series
best_for.skip_html: if you want a full orchestra or a choir: this is organ, one voice and a flute

items.a: St Stephen's Basilica, Szent István tér 1, 1051 Budapest.

VIP (row 1), Cat. I (rows 2–6), Cat. II (rows 7–16), Cat. III (rows 17–26).
Teleki Miklós (organ), Kolos Kováts (bass), Eleonóra Krusic (flute).
Trio format, no orchestra or choir. Rows run back to row 26, a long way from the players. Listed length varies (70–130 minutes), so check the time slot.

pills.label: 65 minutes

pills.label: Wheelchair-friendly

The instrument: Budapest's oldest working organ, in the Baroque St Michael's Church on Váci utca. The organisers describe it as a small instrument, not a huge cathedral organ, and the programme suits it: Bach, Handel, Mozart, Franck.
Who plays: Miklós Teleki, the series' creative director, who gives about 120 recitals a year, with soprano Zita Szilágyi on vocal dates. Some dates are solo organ or chamber music instead.

pills.summary_html: 📺 Screen on the organist▾
pills.pop_html: Why it matters: a screen shows the organist playing, and there is a short introduction in English and Hungarian plus a printed leaflet.
Seating: free seating. The old pews are heated, the chairs are more comfortable. No seat categories, so arrive early for the front.

pills.label: What's included
pills.pop_html: Included: Entry tickets; Organ concert on the oldest working organ in Budapest; St Michael's Church, Budapest; Programme leaflet and introduction in English.Not included: Guide; Transport.

pills.label: Skip the ticket queue
pills.pop_html: Skip the ticket queue: your entry is booked in advance.

best_for.pick_html: for organ lovers on a budget, because €23 buys a 65-minute Bach-to-Franck programme on the city's oldest working organ, with a screen so you can watch the organist play
best_for.skip_html: if you want the grand scale of the Basilica or monumental organ pieces; this organ is small by design

Free seating; heated pews or chairs.

Who plays: the Budapest Classic Orchestra with a violin soloist and a soprano. The only church concert under €30 here with an orchestra rather than an organ.

Programme: Vivaldi's Spring and Summer, Pachelbel's Canon, Mozart's Lacrimosa, Bach's Air on the G String, Schubert's Ave Maria, Mozart's Salzburg Symphony, Beethoven's 5th (Allegro) and Handel's Ombra mai fu.
Timing: doors open 15 minutes before the start. Late arrivals are let in between pieces, so a delay does not cost you the whole concert.
Location: Szervita tér 6, a few steps from Váci utca in the centre of Pest, easy to pair with dinner in District V.

pills.label: What's included
pills.pop_html: Included: Entrance ticket; Printed concert programme; Violin solo; Soprano singer.Not included: Transport.

best_for.pick_html: for first-timers who want the famous tunes, because €28 gets you an orchestra, a violin soloist and a soprano playing Vivaldi, Bach, Mozart and Beethoven in one hour
best_for.skip_html: if you came to hear a church organ; there is none in this programme

Who performs: a professional ensemble founded in 1950, staging Hungarian folk dance and music in costume. Two 30-minute halves with a 20-minute break.

pills.summary_html: 🍽️ Show, soup or dinner▾
pills.pop_html: Options: the cheapest option is the show with a drink. The listing's options add soup or a 3-course dinner: chicken paprikash with Somlói sponge cake, or a vegetarian menu (request it when booking).
Timeline: arrival and welcome drink 18:30–19:00, first half 19:00–19:30, break 19:30–19:50, second half 19:50–20:20.
Access: the cellar venue on Király utca is not wheelchair-accessible and not suitable for people with mobility impairments.

pills.label: 1 hour

pills.label: Not step-free

What you see: the auditorium frescoes and the grand staircase of the Opera House, built in 1884 to Miklós Ybl's plans and fully restored in 2022. Tours can be cancelled for rehearsals; you are then offered another date.
The music: a short live performance on the landing of the grand staircase at the end of the tour. It is a finale, not a full concert.
Tour languages: English, German, French, Italian and Spanish, with a live guide. Pick the language when you book.

pills.summary_html: 🎟️ Skip the ticket queue▾
pills.pop_html: Entry: meet in the Opera House on Andrássy út 22. The ticket skips the ticket-office line; it is not suitable for wheelchair users.

pills.label: What's included
pills.pop_html: Included: Interior visit to the Opera House; Live guide; 60-minute tour; Brief concert.Not included: Food and drinks.

best_for.pick_html: for architecture and opera fans with a free hour, because €33 gets you inside the restored 1884 Opera House plus a short live performance on the staircase
best_for.skip_html: if you want a real concert: the music is a brief finale, and the opera itself needs a separate show ticket

pills.label: 1 hour–70 minutes
pills.pop_html: Duration: 1 hour–70 minutes.

Choose by date: Mozart's Requiem in D minor in full, an organ concert (Bach Toccata, Widor Toccata, Handel, Gounod and Schubert Ave Maria), or an Ave Maria / Air / Alleluja programme with Vivaldi's Winter.
Seating: four seating classes priced separately, so you can trade view for budget. The from-price is €60.
Access: the Basilica concerts are listed as wheelchair-accessible, unlike the Opera tour and the Rajkó cellar show.

pills.summary_html: 📅 30 Dec moves venue▾
pills.pop_html: Watch the date: the 30 December concert takes place in Matthias Church on Castle Hill, not in the Basilica. 25 and 31 December have their own programme.

best_for.skip_html: if you only want organ music in the Basilica: #1 does that for €26

pills.label: 2 hours
pills.pop_html: Duration: 2 hours.

The menu: traditional: goulash in a cauldron, chicken paprikash with egg dumplings, Somló sponge trifle. Vegan: green pea soup, vegan stuffed cabbage, chocolate cake with raspberry mousse. You choose on site.
Drinks: a glass of sparkling wine or orange juice to start. Every other drink is ordered and paid for separately.
The show: two 15-minute folklore sets in costume with live folk music all evening, then you can learn a few dance steps.
Seating: tables seat 4 or 6. On busy nights you may share with another booking; tell them in advance if separate bookings want to sit together.

pills.label: What's included
pills.pop_html: Included: Three-course Hungarian dinner (Traditional or Vegan); Welcome sparkling wine or orange juice; Two 15-minute live folklore performances; Live Hungarian folk music throughout the evening; Learn a few traditional dance steps after the show.

best_for.pick_html: for couples and families who want dinner to be the main event, because €55 covers a full 3-course Hungarian meal with live folk music around you all evening
best_for.skip_html: if you want a long dance show: the folklore sets total 30 minutes
